topics.title: Matrix, order and types
notes: A matrix is an ordered rectangular array of numbers. With m rows and n columns it has order m × n (rows × columns).
Row matrix: one row (1 × n). Column matrix: one column (m × 1). Zero matrix: all elements 0.
Square matrix: rows = columns (n × n). Diagonal matrix: square, all non-diagonal elements 0.
Scalar matrix: diagonal matrix with all diagonal elements equal. Identity (unit) matrix I: scalar matrix with all diagonal elements 1.

topics.title: Triangular, transpose and symmetric matrices
notes: Upper triangular: all entries below the diagonal are 0. Lower triangular: all entries above the diagonal are 0.
Transpose Aᵀ: rows and columns interchanged. If A is m × n then Aᵀ is n × m.
Symmetric matrix: A = Aᵀ. Only square matrices can be symmetric.

topics.title: Addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication
notes: Addition and subtraction are possible only when both matrices have the same order. Add or subtract element by element.
Scalar multiplication: multiply every element by the same number k: kA.

topics.title: Matrix multiplication
notes: A·B is possible only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B.
If A is m × n and B is n × r, then A·B is m × r.
Matrix multiplication is generally NOT commutative: AB ≠ BA in general.
A² = A·A. Example: for A = [[0, 1], [1, 0]], A² = I.

topics.title: Determinant of 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 matrices
notes: Determinant |A| (or det A) is defined only for square matrices.
3 × 3: expand along a row or column: |A| = a11·M11 − a12·M12 + a13·M13 (cofactor expansion).
|AB| = |A|·|B| for square matrices of the same order.

topics.title: Minors and cofactors
notes: Minor M_ij of an element a_ij: determinant of the matrix left after deleting row i and column j.
Cofactor C_ij = (−1)^(i+j) · M_ij. Signs for a 3 × 3 matrix: + − + / − + − / + − +.
The minor matrix has M_ij in each position; the cofactor matrix has C_ij in each position.

topics.title: Adjoint of a matrix
notes: Adjoint adj(A) = transpose of the cofactor matrix: adj(A) = Cᵀ.
For a 2 × 2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]]: adj(A) = [[d, −b], [−c, a]] (swap the diagonal, change the sign of the other two).
The adjoint is used to find the inverse.

topics.title: Inverse of a matrix
notes: A⁻¹ exists only when |A| ≠ 0 (non-singular matrix). Then A·A⁻¹ = I.
Formula: A⁻¹ = adj(A) / |A|.
For a 2 × 2 matrix: A⁻¹ = (1/|A|) [[d, −b], [−c, a]].

short.q: Define the order of a matrix. What is the order of [[1, 2, 3]]?
short.answer: Order = rows × columns. [[1, 2, 3]] has 1 row and 3 columns, so its order is 1 × 3 (a row matrix).

short.q: Define a symmetric matrix and give a 2 × 2 example.
short.answer: A is symmetric if A = Aᵀ. Example: [[1, 4], [4, 7]].

short.q: Show that A² = I for A = [[0, 1], [1, 0]].
Define the minor and the cofactor of an element a_ij.
short.answer: Minor M_ij is the determinant after deleting row i and column j. Cofactor C_ij = (−1)^(i+j) · M_ij.

short.q: State the formula for the inverse of a matrix and when it exists.
short.answer: A⁻¹ = adj(A) / |A|. It exists only when |A| ≠ 0.
